narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Ledger Desk"**

SIMRS-Flow looks like a billing clerk's desk: warm ruled paper, blue ink, and a monospace
hand for anything that is a number, an ID or a status. The operator is checking money and
patient records, so the interface stays calm and precise. Every state is written down
plainly, and nothing competes with the data for attention.

The system is dense but not cramped:
- Thin rules separate everything.
- Corners are nearly square.
- Section headers are numbered like ledger entries ("01 ·").
- Colour is mostly reserved for meaning: ink blue for the action and the current place,
  and green, amber, red and violet for workflow state.

The paper theme is the default. A night theme ("Night Ledger") keeps the same structure
on deep navy for dim rooms.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper canvas, one blue ink accent, semantic status colours.
General Sans for reading; IBM Plex Mono for labels, data, IDs and timestamps.
Hairline rules and near-square corners; pills only for status chips.
Restrained motion: short eases on colour, border and a 2px lift.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Ledger Ink is the only accent hue. Anything blue means "action" or "you are here". Never use it as decoration.

rules.name: The Written-State Rule
rules.body: A status colour never appears without its word. Chips and nodes always carry a text label (Selesai, Menunggu, RUNNING), so meaning survives colour-blindness and grayscale printouts.

rules.name: The Counted-Things-Are-Mono Rule
rules.body: If an operator might compare it against SIMRS (an ID, a date, an amount, a status code), set it in IBM Plex Mono. Prose stays in General Sans.

rules.name: The Mixed-Language Rule
rules.body: Control labels stay in English (Run, Preview, Inspector). Domain terms and statuses stay in Bahasa Indonesia (Rawat Inap, Berjalan, Selesai). Typography treats both the same; never translate one side to "match".

rules.name: The Every-Screen-Is-A-Work-Screen Rule
rules.body: The layout must not scroll sideways and must keep every task reachable from below 1366×768 up to 2560px. Phones and tablets get the stacked Run layout, not a cut-down one.

rules.name: The Lift-On-Intent Rule
rules.body: Cards rise only 2px on hover (`--lift`, eased over .32s). Depth reacts to the operator; it never animates on its own.

dos: Do keep Ledger Ink as the single accent. Status colours carry state only.
Do give every action that writes to SIMRS the amber warning tone, so a write never looks like a routine click.
Do set IDs, no. RM, money, dates and statuses in IBM Plex Mono.
Do pair every status colour with its word, in both themes.
Do keep corners at 0–3px, and use pills only for status and presence chips.
Do keep section headers as uppercase mono with the automatic ledger number.
Do keep sticky or overlay surfaces opaque, so content scrolling underneath never shows through.
Do verify every layout from below 1366×768 to 2560px and on a phone, in both paper and night themes.
donts: Don't fill status chips with solid colour. They stay tinted with a hairline border.
Don't add a second accent hue or use blue decoratively.
Don't use grid backgrounds outside the workflow canvas.
Don't let floating Run panels cover the graph toolbar or each other in the default layout.
Don't convey preview versus write by colour alone. Write mode always says "Confirmed write" and uses the amber tone.
